instruction:
Overview: This task covers a four-paper evolution chain of ns-3 RDMA congestion-control simulators, all sharing the same qbb (Queue-Building-Block) RDMA framework. You will implement each paper's contributions in its own directory, progressively building from DCQCN's ECN-based rate control to HPCC's INT-based precision, then TLT-RDMA's timeout-less transport, and finally ConWeave's load-balanced multipath RDMA.

Directory layout:

`/workspace/dcqcn/` — base framework already present here, start here
`/workspace/hpcc/` — create by copying from dcqcn after finishing it
`/workspace/tlt_rdma/` — create by copying from hpcc after finishing it
`/workspace/conweave/` — create by copying from tlt_rdma after finishing it

Implementation order:

1. Implement ALL mechanisms of Paper 1 (DCQCN) inside `/workspace/dcqcn/`
2. Copy it as the base for Paper 2:
   `cp -r /workspace/dcqcn/ /workspace/hpcc/`
3. Implement ALL of Paper 2's NEW mechanisms (HPCC) on top, inside `/workspace/hpcc/`
4. Copy it as the base for Paper 3:
   `cp -r /workspace/hpcc/ /workspace/tlt_rdma/`
5. Implement ALL of Paper 3's NEW mechanisms (TLT-RDMA) on top, inside `/workspace/tlt_rdma/`
6. Copy it as the base for Paper 4:
   `cp -r /workspace/tlt_rdma/ /workspace/conweave/`
7. Implement ALL of Paper 4's NEW mechanisms (ConWeave) on top, inside `/workspace/conweave/`

DAG units: The task now uses paper-level implementation units with matching requirement files under `requirements/`: `dcqcn`, `hpcc`, `tlt_rdma`, and `conweave`.

Each paper directory must end up as a complete, working implementation, not
just a patch containing that paper's new additions. Implement the mechanisms
described for each stage in full.

---

Paper 1: dcqcn — Congestion Control for Large-Scale RDMA Deployments (SIGCOMM 2015)

Working directory: `/workspace/dcqcn/`

Mechanisms to implement (implement ALL of the following):

ECN Marking at Switch: The switch marks packets with ECN when the queue length exceeds Kmin/Kmax thresholds. Use RED-style probabilistic marking between Kmin and Kmax; mark all packets above Kmax. Thresholds scale with link bandwidth.

CNP Generation at Receiver: When a receiver's NIC sees an ECN-marked packet, it generates a CNP (Congestion Notification Packet) and sends it back to the sender. Rate-limit CNPs to at most once per RTT per QP to avoid flooding.

Rate Decrease at Sender (on CNP): On receiving a CNP, the sender: (1) Updates alpha: `α ← (1 - g) × α + g × 1` where g = 1/256 by default; (2) Decreases current rate: `Rc ← Rc × (1 - α/2)`; (3) Saves rate as target: `Rt ← Rc`.

Rate Increase (Fast Recovery + Active Increase): After a timer period T without a CNP: Fast Recovery phase: `Rc ← (Rc + Rt) / 2` (repeated up to 5 times); then Additive Increase: `Rc ← Rc + RAI` (where RAI is the rate additive increment). Alpha decays during recovery: `α ← (1 - g) × α`.

Alpha Initialization: New flows start with `α = 1` (maximum congestion assumed), decaying toward 0 as CNPs stop arriving.

PFC (Priority Flow Control): Lossless Ethernet mechanism: when a switch's queue exceeds a threshold, it sends a PAUSE frame to upstream NICs to halt transmission on that priority class temporarily. Implement both pause and resume logic.

ns-3 Build and Run: The simulator uses Python 2 waf as the build system. Build with `python waf configure --build-profile=optimized && python waf -j$(nproc)`. Run experiments with `python run.py --cc dcqcn --bw 100 --topo topology --trace flow`.

Experiments to run (run from `/workspace/dcqcn/`):

`dcqcn_queue_len_incast`: Run 2:1 incast simulation (2 senders, each sending a 200 MB flow to 1 receiver simultaneously via a 100 Gbps switch). Measure the maximum switch queue length (bytes) observed across all ports during the monitoring window. Parse `mix/qlen_topology_flow_dcqcn.txt`: each data line has format `<switch_id> <port_id> <count_0KB> <count_1KB> ...`, where count[i] = number of samples with queue at i KB. The max queue = last non-zero index × 1000 bytes. Output: a single integer (bytes).

`dcqcn_fct_incast_us`: Using the same 2:1 incast simulation output, compute the average Flow Completion Time (FCT) in microseconds for the 2 flows. Parse `mix/fct_topology_flow_dcqcn.txt`: each line has fields `sip dip sport dport size_bytes start_ns fct_ns standalone_fct_ns`. Column 7 (0-indexed: column index 6) is the FCT in nanoseconds. Average all FCTs and convert to microseconds (divide by 1000). Output: a floating-point value in microseconds.

---

Paper 2: hpcc — HPCC: High Precision Congestion Control (SIGCOMM 2019)

Working directory: `/workspace/hpcc/`
Base: copy from your completed `/workspace/dcqcn/` first.

Mechanisms to implement (implement ALL of the following — including inherited ones from Paper 1):

DCQCN (inherited from Paper 1): ECN marking, CNP generation, rate decrease/increase, alpha update, PFC — all already present after the `cp -r` from dcqcn.

INT Header (per-hop telemetry): Each packet carries an INT header populated by every switch on the path. Per-hop fields: `txRate` (egress port transmission rate, bits/sec), `B` (link bandwidth, bits/sec), `qLen` (queue length in bytes), and `ts` (timestamp). The receiver's ACK carries this INT data back to the sender.

Utilization Computation at Sender: On receiving an ACK with H hops of INT data, for each hop i compute: `u_i = (txRate_i + qLen_i / τ) / B_i` where τ = base RTT estimate. Use the maximum utilization: `U = max(u_0, ..., u_{H-1})`.

Rate Update (HPCC algorithm, cc_mode=3): On each ACK: If `U >= η` (target utilization, default η=0.95): `W_new = W / U + W_AI / B` If `U < η`: `W_new = W + W_AI / B` where W = congestion window (bytes), W_AI = additive increment, B = link bandwidth. Actual sending rate: `R = W / RTT`.

Switch Model Extension (INT insertion): Compared to DCQCN, add per-switch logic to insert INT fields into packet headers when forwarding. Track per-egress-port transmission rate and queue length for INT reporting.

Fast Startup: New flows start at line rate; the INT-based control converges downward within 1–2 RTTs if congestion is detected (no slow start).

Build and Run: Same waf build system as dcqcn. Run with: `python run.py --cc hp --bw 100 --topo topology --trace flow`.

Experiments to run (run from `/workspace/hpcc/`):

`hpcc_max_queue_len_bytes`: Run the same 2:1 incast scenario (2 × 200 MB flows at 100 Gbps) with HPCC (cc=hp). Measure the maximum switch queue length (bytes). Parse `mix/qlen_topology_flow_hp95.txt` using the same method as dcqcn_queue_len_incast (last non-zero KB index × 1000). Output: a single integer (bytes). Should be dramatically lower than DCQCN's value.

---

Paper 3: tlt_rdma — Towards Timeout-Less Transport (EuroSys 2021)

Working directory: `/workspace/tlt_rdma/`
Base: copy from your completed `/workspace/hpcc/` first.

Mechanisms to implement (implement ALL of the following):

DCQCN and HPCC (inherited): All rate control and telemetry from Papers 1 and 2 are already present after the `cp -r` from hpcc.

Receiver-Side Out-of-Order Detection: The receiver NIC tracks the expected next sequence number for each QP. When a gap is detected (expected seq ≠ received seq), immediately send a NACK without waiting for any timer.

NACK Packet Type: Add a new RDMA packet type (NACK) carrying the QP identifier and the missing sequence number. Rate-limit NACK generation to at most 1 per RTT per gap to prevent NACK storms.

Sender-Side Selective Retransmission: On receiving a NACK, retransmit only the missing packet (selective retransmission). Do NOT reduce the congestion window on a NACK — retransmission due to loss does not indicate congestion. Maintain a per-QP retransmit queue for unacknowledged packets.

RTO Elimination: Remove the go-back-N retransmission timeout (RTO) timer from the NIC model entirely. The NACK mechanism handles all loss recovery. A coarse watchdog timer for dead-connection detection may remain, but the RTO for data retransmission must be eliminated.

Config file: Place simulation parameters in `mix/config_tlt_exp.txt`. Key settings: `ENABLE_TLT 1` to enable timeout-less transport, `ERROR_RATE_PER_LINK 0.001` (0.1% random packet loss to trigger retransmission paths), and dumbbell topology parameters. Run with: `./waf --run 'scratch/hpcc-dumbbell mix/config_tlt_exp.txt'`.

Experiments to run (run from `/workspace/tlt_rdma/`):

`tlt_timeout_events`: Run the dumbbell simulation with `ENABLE_TLT 1` and `ERROR_RATE_PER_LINK 0.001`. Count the total number of RTO (retransmission timeout) events across all NICs. Parse the simulation stdout: sum all values in column 4 (0-indexed: index 3) from lines matching `L2_RTO`. Line format: `<time>\tL2_RTO\t<nic_ptr>\t<count>`. Output: a single integer. Expected: 0 (TLT eliminates all timeouts).

---

Paper 4: conweave — Network Load Balancing with In-network Reordering Support (SIGCOMM 2023)

Working directory: `/workspace/conweave/`
Base: copy from your completed `/workspace/tlt_rdma/` first.

Mechanisms to implement (implement ALL of the following):

Inherited mechanisms: DCQCN, HPCC, TLT-RDMA transport — all already present after the `cp -r` from tlt_rdma.

Path Spray at Switch (ConWeave routing): Replace per-flow ECMP path selection with fine-grained packet-level load balancing. The switch maintains per-port byte counters and selects the egress port with the lowest current utilization from the ECMP group. Use a configurable monitoring interval to update utilization estimates.

Receiver-Side Reorder Buffer: Since packets from the same flow may arrive out of order (traveling different paths), implement a per-QP reorder buffer at the receiver. Hold packets that arrive out of sequence; release them to the application only when all prior packets have arrived. Use a sliding window mechanism.

PAUSE/RESUME Protocol (per-QP flow control): When the reorder buffer exceeds its capacity, the receiver sends a PAUSE message to the sender (per-QP, not PFC which is per-port). The sender halts transmission until a RESUME is received. This prevents buffer overflow without triggering link-level PFC.

New Packet Headers: Add ConWeave-specific header fields for PAUSE/RESUME signaling and path spray coordination. The network-load-balance simulation entry point uses `scratch/network-load-balance.cc`.

Build and Run: Same waf build system. Run with: `python3 run.py --lb conweave --pfc 1 --irn 0 --simul_time 0.015 --netload 50 --topo leaf_spine_128_100G_OS2`. The simulation uses cc=dcqcn (cc_mode=1) with lb=conweave (lb_mode=9).

Experiments to run (run from `/workspace/conweave/`):

`conweave_load_balance_utilization`: Run ConWeave simulation on a leaf-spine 128-host topology at 50% network load for 15ms with ConWeave load balancing enabled. Parse the uplink monitoring file (`mix/output/<id>/<id>_out_uplink.txt`) which records per-port byte counts at 10µs intervals. Line format: `<timestamp_ns>,<switch_id>,<port_id>,<cumulative_bytes>`. Compute per-switch throughput imbalance: for each 100µs window, group uplink ports by switch and compute `(MAX_bytes - MIN_bytes) / AVG_bytes * 100` for each switch. Exclude windows where AVG is 0. Report the median imbalance value (%) across all valid switch-window combinations. Skip the first 5ms of the monitoring window as warm-up (use timestamps starting at 2005000000 ns). Output: a floating-point value in percent.

---

run.sh Specification

After implementing all papers, write `/workspace/run.sh` that:
0. Materializes `/workspace/hpcc/`, `/workspace/tlt_rdma/`, and `/workspace/conweave/` in paper order before running experiments (for example by copying the prior paper and overlaying the next paper's deltas).
1. Runs ALL experiments for ALL papers
2. Writes results to `/workspace/results.json` in this exact format:
   {
     "dcqcn": {
       "dcqcn_queue_len_incast": <numeric_value>,
       "dcqcn_fct_incast_us": <numeric_value>
     },
     "hpcc": {
       "hpcc_max_queue_len_bytes": <numeric_value>
     },
     "tlt_rdma": {
       "tlt_timeout_events": <numeric_value>
     },
     "conweave": {
       "conweave_load_balance_utilization": <numeric_value>
     }
   }
3. Working directories:
   dcqcn experiments: `cd /workspace/dcqcn/`
   hpcc experiments: `cd /workspace/hpcc/`
   tlt_rdma experiments: `cd /workspace/tlt_rdma/`
   conweave experiments: `cd /workspace/conweave/`
4. Total experiment count in `results.json` must equal 5
5. All values must be numeric (int or float)

moduleDag.project: DCQCN RDMA Congestion Control Evolution Chain
moduleDag.description: A four-paper evolution chain of ns-3 RDMA congestion-control simulators sharing the same QBB (Queue-Building-Block) framework. Starting from DCQCN's ECN-based rate control (SIGCOMM 2015), evolving to HPCC's INT-based precision (SIGCOMM 2019), then TLT-RDMA's timeout-less transport (EuroSys 2021), and finally ConWeave's congestion-aware multipath load balancing (SIGCOMM 2023). Each paper directory is created by copying the previous paper and adding incremental mechanisms.

nodes.label: QBB RDMA Base Framework
nodes.description: The ns-3 simulation framework providing the foundational RDMA infrastructure: QBB net device, queue pairs, RDMA driver, switch MMU, PFC pause/resume, custom headers, INT header structures, point-to-point channels, and the simulation entry point (scratch/third.cc). Contains TODO stubs for congestion control algorithms. Includes run.py launcher, mix/ config and topology files, and the waf build system.

nodes.label: DCQCN Rate Control (Paper 1)
nodes.description: Implements the DCQCN (Data Center QCN) congestion control algorithm in rdma-hw.cc: alpha update with EWMA, CNP reception handler, rate decrease on congestion (Rc = Rc*(1-alpha/2)), fast recovery (averaging toward target), active increase (additive), and hyper increase phases. Also implements HPCC INT-based rate control (cc_mode=3) with per-hop utilization computation.

nodes.label: Switch ECN Marking and INT Insertion (Paper 1+2)
nodes.description: Implements ECN marking at the switch using RED-style probabilistic marking between Kmin/Kmax thresholds, and INT header insertion for HPCC (PushHop with timestamp, txBytes, queue length, and line rate). Enables switches to populate per-hop telemetry for INT-based congestion control.

nodes.label: HPCC INT-Based Control (Paper 2)
nodes.description: Logical paper-copy unit for the hpcc/ directory. In this task representation there is no unique file delta beyond the shared dcqcn source changes: HPCC's INT-aware rdma-hw.cc and switch-node.cc logic already lives in the shared dcqcn tree, and hpcc/ is materialized as a copy of the completed dcqcn/ directory during the final integration run.

nodes.label: TLT-RDMA Timeout-Less Transport (Paper 3)
nodes.description: Overlay files for the TLT-RDMA paper's root/transport delta relative to HPCC. This unit owns the point-to-point transport changes, the transport- scoped repo metadata files, and the delete manifest applied when the final run materializes a full tlt_rdma/ directory from hpcc/.

nodes.label: TLT Network Utils and Applications (Paper 3)
nodes.description: Overlay files for the TLT-RDMA network/application layer delta relative to HPCC, including custom-header NACK support, updated queue helpers, and the application-side helpers used by the dumbbell experiments.

nodes.label: TLT Simulation Programs and Config (Paper 3)
nodes.description: Overlay files for TLT-RDMA's simulation drivers and configs, including hpcc-dumbbell.cc, config_tlt_exp.txt, and the run.py helper used to materialize and exercise the timeout-less transport experiments.

nodes.label: ConWeave Load-Balance Routing (Paper 4)
nodes.description: Overlay files for ConWeave's point-to-point/routing delta relative to TLT-RDMA. This unit owns the routing logic, VOQ support, and root-level repo metadata that get overlaid when the final run materializes conweave/ from the completed tlt_rdma/ tree.

nodes.label: ConWeave Network and Application Layer (Paper 4)
nodes.description: Overlay files for ConWeave's network/application layer delta, including updated packet headers, uplink accounting helpers, and UDP helper changes needed by the leaf-spine experiments.

nodes.label: ConWeave Simulation and Analysis (Paper 4)
nodes.description: Overlay files for ConWeave's simulation/analysis delta relative to TLT-RDMA, including network-load-balance.cc, the leaf_spine_128_100G_OS2 config, run.py, workload assets, analysis scripts, and the delete manifest used when the final run materializes a full conweave/ tree.

nodes.label: Experiment Runner (run.sh)
nodes.description: Top-level experiment orchestration script that builds each paper's ns-3 simulator, runs the designated experiments (dcqcn incast, hpcc queue measurement, tlt timeout counting, conweave load-balance utilization), parses output files, and writes results.json with all 5 experiment metrics.
